case_name: OTRF APT29 Day 1 SCRANTON to NASHUA emulation
date_metadata_note: The day1 README records 2020-04-29 while the parent APT29 README records 2020-05-01 for the host package. The conservative envelope below covers both and is not an exact attack-window claim.
window_semantics: preinspection conservative ingestion envelope; do not narrow after reading events to improve motif recovery
ground_truth_summary: The emulation starts with user execution on SCRANTON, establishes Pupy and Meterpreter command-and-control, collects and exfiltrates data, deploys a stealth toolkit with a UAC bypass, establishes persistence, steals credentials, moves laterally to NASHUA, and performs a second collection and exfiltration sequence.

multiclaim_gate.failure_rule: Keep the node unsupported under AND; do not replace the frozen step after event inspection.

actor_label_boundary: APT29 is the emulated scenario label. It is not an unknown actor prediction target and cannot be scored as actor attribution correctness.
data_quality_notes: Host and network sources are independently packaged but originate from the same emulation run.
The repository is suitable for cross-sensor corroboration, not for estimating prevalence in operational APT incidents.
No event count, event identifier, provider distribution, exact timestamp, or recovered motif is asserted before archive inspection.
notes: Selected after all C07-C10 planner parameters were frozen. C11 may close the third-data-family engineering gap only after source and compilation Gates pass; it cannot by itself close human granularity validity or real-world attribution validity.
